conflicts_noticed: ETH Zurich tuition (ethz-msc-cs): https://ethz.ch/en/studies/financial.html says 'ETH tuition and semester fees sum up to CHF 804/semester.' (no fee groups mentioned), while https://ethz.ch/students/en/studies/financial/tuition-fees.html says 'Threefold tuition fee: CHF 2190 / semester' for everyone who does not qualify for the simple fee (CHF 730), which includes typical Pakistani applicants. Both are proposed. The 804 figure appears to be the simple-fee total and is likely outdated or misleading for international applicants.

TUM tuition (tum-msc-informatics), a pending change rather than a second value: the program page states 6,000 euros per semester, but https://www.tum.de/en/studies/fees/tuition says Master's fees for non-EU students rise for the winter semester 2027/28 to 4,600 or 6,800 euros per semester. Neither band equals 6,000, and the fee page does not say which band Informatics falls in. Only 6,000 is proposed; WS 2027/28 starters will probably pay a different amount.

rejected.reason: Official TUM fee page (tum.de/en/studies/fees/tuition) says non-EU Master's fees for students starting in WS 2027/28 rise to 4,600 or 6,800 EUR/semester. 6,000 is the current rate, not valid for the WS 2027/28 intake this deadline targets, and the page does not say which band Informatics gets.

The cited TUM language page explicitly accepts proof of English through an English-taught Bachelor's (at least 50%) and, for CIT programmes, an English Bachelor's thesis. The value sets waiver null and the notes wrongly say no such route exists, which would push Pakistani applicants into a paid test they may not need.

The value keeps only the lower bound of the published CHF 20,000-26,000 p.a. range, and that range is for 'living and study costs', not living alone. It understates the cost and can double-count with tuition.

Not the same field or applicant group. CHF 804 is tuition plus semester fees and matches the simple-fee group (CHF 730 + fees); Pakistani applicants pay the threefold fee of CHF 2190 per the official tuition-fees page. Not a genuine conflict.

2.5 is only the direct-admission threshold. The page says applicants with a worse grade can still be admitted through an oral aptitude test (its table covers grades up to 4.0). GpaRule.min means the worst acceptable grade, so 2.5 would wrongly mark eligible students 'Below minimum'.

The course page lists a Round 4 (opens 11 Mar 2027, closes 28 Apr 2027), and the notes wrongly call Round 3 the final round. 10 Mar 2027 is neither the next deadline (6 Jan 2027) nor the final one (28 Apr 2027).

75% is Imperial's university-wide floor for Pakistan. The course page says those standards 'are the minimum for entry to Imperial, and not specifically this Department', and the course needs a First-Class degree in a non-computing subject. It would show 'Meets minimum' to students who do not qualify.

The inference is unsupported. 'Need to meet specific requirements to progress' describes conditional progression and says nothing about whether a place is guaranteed once the requirements are met. No QMUL page checked states either way, so this should stay Not verified.

12 months covers only the Pre-Masters stage, and its own term dates run about 6-7 months. The seed program is the whole 'Pre-Master's + MSc' route (about 24 months with the 1-year Conversion MSc), so the value understates study time.

£25,950 is the Pre-Masters fee only. With period 'total' the app would treat it as the whole route's tuition and leave out the £33,150 overseas fee for MSc Computer Science (Conversion, Sept 2027), so it understates tuition by more than half.
